rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off track on every track (oval, s-bend, slalom). Progress was only 0.11 to 0.17, so the robot leaves the tape within the first half metre. Max error (0.061 to 0.066) exceeds the off-track limit of about 0.0575 m, while RMS error (0.03 to 0.034) and steering oscillation (0.07 to 0.17) are small. The robot is therefore drifting outward at a steady rate rather than oscillating. Line-loss events (1 to 2) show the line leaves the sensor array during these excursions. Likely causes: (a) base_speed 1.6 is too fast for the bends and the steering response lags; (b) ki = 0 leaves the constant left/right motor mismatch uncorrected, so the robot carries a steady offset that accumulates on curves; (c) the sensors at y = 0.03 see the line late, so the controller reacts after the wheels are already off line.

Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 -> 1.2 to give the controller time to correct on bends, which is the main fix for surviving the track; the finish-time term is secondary to not leaving the line. (2) kp 3.0 -> 4.0 for a stronger correction of offset. (3) ki 0 -> 0.2 to cancel the fixed motor mismatch. The integral is capped at ±2, so the turn contribution stays bounded at 0.4. (4) kd 0.2 -> 0.6 to damp the faster kp response. (5) Sensors moved forward to y = 0.05 for look-ahead, and spread to x = ±0.03 (spacing 1.5 cm, 12 mm footprint) so the array keeps seeing tape through wider bends. (6) Mass 0.8 -> 0.6 kg to reduce yaw inertia so the robot turns more quickly. Body and wheel geometry are otherwise unchanged. Body width stays at 0.18 m, the maximum, which gives the widest off-track allowance (0.0575 m).

Expected result: nonzero completion on the oval and s-bend, with progress well above 0.2 and line-loss events near zero. Completion within 3 s may not occur at 1.2 speed, so completion time is the trade-off to watch. Hypotheses to check next: (H1) the off-track failures come mainly from speed, so progress should rise sharply when base_speed drops. (H2) ki removes the steady drift, so rms_error should fall. (H3) the forward sensors reduce line-loss events. If the robot now oscillates (steering_oscillation rising sharply), reduce kp to about 3 and keep kd. If it survives but is too slow, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 while watching max_error.
